sources.title: Quran 5:6
sources.supports: The verse names the washed and wiped parts and distinguishes major purification.

sources.title: Dar al-Ifta: How to perform wudhu
sources.supports: The practical guide describes intention in the heart, the sequence, ears and coverage of fingers and toes.

sources.title: Sahih al-Bukhari 159
sources.supports: The report describes washing the hands, face, forearms and feet three times, mouth and nose cleaning and head wiping.

sources.title: Sahih al-Bukhari 185
sources.supports: The reported head wiping goes from the front to the back and returns to the starting point.

sources.title: Dar al-Ifta: Mouth rinsing and implanted teeth
sources.supports: The discussion names the majority Sunnah classification for mouth rinsing in wudu and the relied-upon Hanbali obligation.

sources.title: Dar al-Ifta: Differences between schools in purification
sources.supports: The discussion distinguishes Maliki rubbing of washed limbs from the Shafi‘i classification.

sources.title: Dar al-Ifta: Mentioning God’s name in the bathroom
sources.supports: The cited institutional answer does not make spoken phrases a validity condition when ablution requirements and intention are fulfilled.

sources.title: Sahih Muslim 234a
sources.supports: The hadith records the testimony of faith after completing ablution.

review.notes: Compared the exact source passages and removed the previous four-obligations-only universal claim, incorrect Bukhari 164 fingernails attribution, unsupported speed claim and blanket nullifier list. Retains existing title/date/authors/images. Distinguishes the named Hanbali mouth-rinsing view and Maliki rubbing example without inventing a complete school chart. Includes the new bleeding answer only after its file exists.
